"Affect vs. Effect  "Affect" is a verb and means to make a difference to. "The cat in the house will probably affect my allergies."   "Effect" is a noun and usually describes the difference itself. "The cat had a profound effect on my allergies."  #NationalGrammarDay #Grammar HTTPURL"

"Capital vs. Capitol  The word, "capital" either refers to money, a city, or uppercase letters. The word, "capitol," however refers to a building.   It is correct to say, "The capitol building is located in the capital city."  #NationalGrammarDay HTTPURL"

"There vs. Their  The word "there" commonly refers to a place or position, such as "over there." If youre showing ownership, use the word, "their."   It is correct to say, "Their house is over there."  #NationalGrammarDay @USER #language #GrammarDay #grammar HTTPURL"

"Its vs. Its  These two words seem pretty easy to figure out, but many people still get them wrong. The word "its" is a contraction for "it is." The word "its" shows possession.   It is correct to say, "Its a fluffy cat and its tail is black."  #NationalGrammarDay HTTPURL"

"Youre vs. Your  The word "youre" is a contraction for "you are."   The word "your" shows possession.   It is correct to say, "Youre nice but your friend is not."  #NationalGrammarDay #Grammar #Language #Learning HTTPURL"
